jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

Reporting to the VP, Credit Modelling & Methodology, the Senior Director, CMM Model Monitoring and Architecture will lead the strategic management of data and the technology infrastructure used for credit parameter development, performance monitoring, and external disclosures.

In this role, the candidate will manage a team that is accountable for the oversight of data used for Wholesale and Retail credit risk parameters. The candidate is also accountable for the performance monitoring of stress and impairment (S&I) models for Canada (IFRS9/EWST) and the US (CECL/CCAR), parameters used in regulatory capital (AIRB), and other CMM-owned models.

The Senior Director is a key leadership position with ownership of data governance for credit modelling and monitoring, and delivering on strategic priorities for CMM from a technology architecture perspective. Successful execution will include close collaboration with model developers, model owners, RBC’s internal lines of defense and regulators.

What will you do?

The Senior Director, supported by a team of 14 - 18, is accountable for:

Developing, documenting, and implementing data and monitoring processes related to parameters used across RBC, including those which drive 80% of RBC’s Risk Weighted Assets as well as all credit Stress Testing & Impairment models.
Rigorous design and execution of SOX controls related to the data used in model development and monitoring. Partnering with other functional areas to ensure adequate data quality controls are in place on upstream data sources.
Leading data governance activities for the CMM team, including the quarterly Data Oversight Working Group, to provide transparency into data quality in critical applications.
Understanding and articulating strategic options with respect to data and performance production, and making strong recommendations to senior management.
Setting and regularly assessing Objectives and Key Results for data management, infrastructure and model monitoring.
Leading the production of external disclosures related to regulatory parameters across retail and wholesale parameters.
Spearheading key stakeholder relationships internally and externally. This includes coaching the team leads how to most effectively partner with colleagues in GRM, lines of business, Internal Audit, External Audit and regulators in Canada and the US.
Driving required outcomes through anticipating and responding to constructive challenges to the output of their team.

What do you need to succeed?

Must-Have

12 – 15+ years work experience in credit risk or a related area with model development, or on-going performance monitoring.
Knowledge of credit risk methodology, including capital estimation, credit risk/stress testing models, and/or direct experience with Expected Credit Loss implementations.
Substantial experience with financial models, regulatory reporting systems, and software implementation.
Experience in managing large datasets and routine production processes subject to a rigorous control environment, and knowledge of best practices in data management.
Experience managing teams and coordinating complex technical projects.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop technical staff.
Knowledge of Python or similar language(s).
Knowledge of modern code development and code management best practices.
Strong interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate and document complex technical problems and control process for a non-technical audience.

Nice-to-Have

Expertise in banking products across retail and wholesale portfolios.
Knowledge of SAS is an asset.
Project management and/or stakeholder coordination experience.
Understanding of SOX controls, internal audit requirements, and regulatory compliance.

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits and competitive compensation
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Flexible work/life balance options
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
Opportunities to do challenging work

Credit Analysis, Financial Regulation, Internal Auditing, Investment Risk Management, Market Risk, Operational Requirements, Operational Risks, Risk Management, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

jobs.title: Director, Operations
jobs.description:
Veritree And Job Overview

veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.

veritree is seeking a Director, Operations to lead our Operations team: the glue that connects our teams and initiatives. Reporting to the COO, you will own veritree's Revenue Ops, Supply Ops, Business Ops, and Business Intelligence functions. These functions empower our Revenue, Forests, Product & Engineering, and Finance teams to operate as one business.

We sell verified trees sourced from planting partners worldwide, alongside new business lines in carbon, monitoring technology licensing, and nonprofit programs. That makes our business closer to a two-sided marketplace than pure SaaS: every customer commitment depends on supply, delivery, and data lining up behind it. As we move to a new AI-native platform, our Operations team is evolving into a team of operations engineers who build the tools, automations, and data flows the business runs on.

This is a hands-on role: you'll run operations first and then evolve the systems behind it. You inherit a capable team and working systems (several of which we've outgrown) and leave behind infrastructure the rest of the company can build upon. The role starts at Director-level, with room for advancement as determined by job performance and business needs.

12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)

Take the wheel: within your first 90 days, run the weekly operations cadence, own escalations across all four functions, and become the decision-maker on operational calls
Operating rhythm: set up how Operations runs for the next stage of the company: a clear meeting rhythm, defined team roles/decision rights, one agreed definition and owner for core metrics (pipeline, ACV, NRR, gross margin, tree inventory), and a 12-month operations roadmap signed off by executive leadership
Trusted data and reporting: keep commercial and delivery data clean across HubSpot, NetSuite, and the platform through go-live and beyond, and produce the monthly reporting pack and the operational metrics in board reporting from the BI stack
AI and automation: ship AI-powered tools and automations that measurably reduce manual work and save costs across the business

What You'll Do

Cross-Functional Operations

Run the operating cadence (meeting cadences, monthly business reviews, semi-annual planning) and the forums where Revenue, Forests, and Product & Engineering align on priorities
Own the deal desk with Sales, Customer Success, and Forests, so what we sell matches what we can deliver
Own the intake, prioritization, and SLA framework for operations requests from every team
Own operational readiness on the platform after go-live: close workflow gaps with Product & Engineering and lead change management
Make operational and commercial decisions within agreed guardrails (pricing, margin floors, custom deliverables), and escalate exceptions to executive leadership with a clear recommendation

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, coach, and develop the Operations team, including managers and individual contributors
Own hiring, onboarding, and ongoing performance management, in partnership with People Operations
Evolve the team into operations engineers by defining roles and scopes and building a culture that is both high-accountability and high-support

Revenue Operations

Own HubSpot as our commercial system of record, including deal stages, order and contract workflows, and clean handoffs between Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Finance
Own the customer revenue forecast and its methodology, in partnership with Finance and Revenue leadership
Own pricing discipline: the price sheet, margin floors, and a quarterly margin and pricing review
Own lead and sales funnel, retention, and unit-economics reporting

Supply Operations

Own demand and supply planning, translating the customer forecast into tree demand by ecosystem and region and partnering with Forests on sourcing and capacity
Own order management, inventory allocation, purchase orders, and fulfillment tracking, including future obligations to customers and planting partners, so every order is delivered on time against the right supply

Business Operations

Own the processes, policies, tooling, and Operations budget that keep the business running, and decide what gets automated and what stays manual
Run the OKR process and tracker, and support annual operating planning
Own the operating model for customer and partner site visits

Business Intelligence & Reporting

Own our data warehouse and BI layer, pulling from HubSpot, NetSuite, the platform, and planting data, as the single source of truth for operational metrics
Direct the team's AI agenda, shipping internal tools, agents, and workflow automations that measurably increase output across the business

Requirements

Qualifications

Professional Requirements Or Qualifications

8+ years in operations, including 3+ years leading a multi-function operations team (at least Revenue Operations and Business Operations) at a B2B company of roughly 75 to 250 people
Experience taking a company from founder-led, ad hoc operations to a repeatable operating system
Experience owning monthly and board-level operational reporting, including the data model and BI layer behind it
Strong HubSpot fluency (you know its strengths and its limits)
Fluency in commercial metrics: NRR, cohorts, funnel conversion, CAC and payback
Experience designing operating processes (intake, SLAs, deal desk) and leading change management for systems people use every day
You have an operating system (cadence, metric tree, single-owner accountability, an intake model) and can articulate it clearly
An AI-native way of working: you already use AI and automation to ship internal tools (e.g., n8n, AI agents)
Excellent written communication, with the ability to make decisions legible to an executive team and a board

Personal Strengths

An operator first: hands-on and low ego
Calm judgment under ambiguity: we're part SaaS, part supply chain, part marketplace, and our model won't fit a template
Pragmatic about data: a high bar on definitions, without waiting for perfect data to act
You learn how a system works before you change it
Genuine passion for sustainability and nature-based solutions

Nice to Haves (not mandatory)

Experience with physical supply or fulfilment (marketplaces, logistics, agriculture)
Experience in supply planning, including demand forecasting, inventory allocation, and capacity constraints
ERP experience, including quote-to-cash
Experience in impact, sustainability, carbon, or nature-based organizations, including grant-funded work or government affairs

Benefits

Benefits & Compensation Overview

At veritree, we recognize that compensation and performance development are key to attracting and retaining top talent. Our approach is grounded in fairness, transparency, and creating opportunities for growth as both our people and business scale.

Some highlights you can expect include:

Competitive salary with a performance-driven framework that ensures fair and consistent compensation reviews, tied to individual impact and business growth
Extended health, dental, and vision benefits
Additional Health Spending Account (HSA) / Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) to support your well-being and lifestyle interests
A variety of time-off programs, including vacation, personal days, and a 4-week remote work program each year
Employee discount with tentree, our sister company
A flexible, hybrid work environment designed for collaboration and focus-driven impact

veritree ensures that compensation is reviewed fairly and consistently, with opportunities for salary progression tied to sustained performance. As such, the salary range for this role including variable compensation is $150,000 to $180,000 CAD.

This range is positioned around the 50th-75th percentile of market data we've collected, reflecting our commitment to competitive pay. Final offer amounts are based on the individual experience and skillset of the candidate demonstrated during the recruitment process.

We reserve the >75th percentile of our salary ranges for internal employees who demonstrate sustained high performance and impact at veritree.

veritree is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that represents diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business needs.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering - VieFund
jobs.description:
About Beacon:

Beacon is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies. They are niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently, accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.

The Role:

VieFund is a Beacon company with remote teams in Toronto, Ottawa and Vietnam. Its software is the system of record for mutual fund, segregated fund and GIC dealers in Canada: advisor tools, trades, settlements, account bookkeeping, and reporting, connected to the industry through FundServ, CANNEX and exempt-market dealer networks.

We are looking for the next technical leader of VieFund. You will own the platform end to end and work closely with the current technical team in Ottawa and Vietnam to build deep knowledge of the product, the dealers, and the operating rhythm. In the first year, you keep every dealer running through tax season, the FundServ standard change, and year-end, and you draw up the plan to move the platform off its on-prem footing, modernize it and add more value to customers with AI. You are the person who understands what is going on quickly and decides what to do about it.

You will be the technical owner of a profitable, long-held product with real customers and real seasonal deadlines, with Beacon's engineering leadership behind you and the mandate to make it better.

What You'll Do:

Own the VieFund platform end to end: architecture, codebase, database, releases, and production operations.
Build and maintain complete documentation of system behaviour, dealer configurations, and operational runbooks.
Maintain and evolve VieFund's FundServ integration, including annual standard upgrades, certification, and resolution of transaction and reconciliation issues with counterparties.
Design, build, and maintain the transaction processing, account bookkeeping, and reporting logic at the core of the product, ensuring accuracy and auditability.
Act as the final escalation point for client-facing technical issues; diagnose root causes and implement durable fixes.
Plan and deliver around the industry calendar, including tax season, RRSP and RRIF deadlines, and regulatory and standards changes.
Define and execute the technical roadmap, including the migration from on-prem infrastructure to the cloud and the adoption of modern engineering and AI-assisted development practices.
Manage production environments across hosted and client-managed Windows Server deployments, including backups, patching, security, and uptime.
Partner with hosting providers, dealers, and internal stakeholders to deliver reliable service and clear communication.
Hire, mentor, and lead engineers and contractors as the team grows.

What we are looking for:

Must have:

Deep, hands-on FundServ experience. Not just sending and receiving files: you have lived through the yearly standard change, you have debugged failures that originated at other vendors or at the fund, and you know how to work the problem when the documentation does not help.
Mutual fund transaction accounting and reporting. You understand the bookkeeping behind trades, settlements, distributions, and corrections, and you have fixed it when it was wrong.
Expert in .NET, MSSQL, and T-SQL. Much of the dealer-specific logic lives in stored procedures and scripts. You are at home there.
Windows Server management. You can stand up, patch, back up, and troubleshoot production servers, including ones you do not control.
Able to be in Ottawa at least bi-weekly for the first six months as part of onboarding. Knowledge transfer happens in person.
Judgment that does not need a committee. You will often be the only engineer in the room.
Easy to work with. Dealers call when something is wrong. The team has to trust you with the product.
Daily use of AI coding tools, and the drive to bring them into a codebase that has none.

Nice to have:

Experience migrating an on-prem system to the cloud, and the judgement to sequence it without breaking customers.
FIX protocol, for the ETF side of the business. Small part of the work, easy to pick up, but a head start helps.
Experience at a Canadian wealth or dealer platform (back office, transfer agency, or dealer software).
Experience replacing a long-tenured sole owner of a system.

Location and Working Arrangement:

Remote with ability to meet with with the teams in Ottawa and/or Toronto, Ontario. During onboarding must be able to be in Ottawa bi-weekly for the first 6 months.
Some work happens outside dealer business hours so it does not disrupt their day. Expect occasional evenings and weekends, heaviest around the seasonal peaks. Reducing this is part of the modernization mandate, but it is the reality today.

Our Values at Beacon Software

Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.
Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.
Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process:
To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions:
Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

At Giant Tiger, our mission is simple: help Canadians save more every day. We’re a Canadian institution rooted in our communities and built on 60+ years of success. As part of our store support team, your work directly impacts stores across the country and drives the value that our customers see on the shelves.

We’re looking for people who are passionate about retail and motivated by meaningful work that makes a real impact. This posting represents a current opportunity at Giant Tiger.

Job Title

Head of Merchandise Operations & Financial Planning

About This Role

Giant Tiger is looking for a strategic merchandise leader to help shape the next chapter of our business as we strengthen our position as a Hard Discount retailer.

This is a significant merchandising leadership role with the opportunity to influence how Giant Tiger plans, operates and delivers value to Canadians. Reporting into our Executive Vice President and Chief Merchant, you will lead Merchandise Operations and Financial Planning, establishing the financial plans, operating rhythms and decision-making frameworks that guide our merchandising business. From sales, margin and inventory planning to pricing, promotions and space productivity, you will help ensure our merchandising strategies translate into disciplined execution, profitable growth and consistently low prices our customers can trust.

Giant Tiger operates differently than Canada's largest retailers. We are a Canadian-owned retailer with more than 260 stores, including a significant franchise network. Our success depends on keeping things simple, making disciplined decisions and ensuring our strategies can be executed consistently across our stores.

Workplace Arrangements

This role will follow a hybrid remote/onsite schedule. Applicants for this role can expect to work on-site from our Ottawa, Ontario Head Office throughout the month.

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Director – Data Solution Delivery, Wealth Management, is accountable for developing, leading, and overseeing the activities of delivery teams responsible for working with cross-functional development teams and business stakeholders to define and implement business strategies, product roadmaps, service offerings, and new features. This is a demanding hands-on and strategic role that requires knowledge of the financial services sector and emerging trends in the Wealth and Asset Management industry.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Take ownership of end-to-end delivery of wealth data exchange engineering use cases and work closely with business and technology stakeholders.
Participate in Data Engineering, Data Architecture strategy, medallion data hub architecture, and roadmap definition and review process.
Demonstrate strong experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) data services and Databricks.
Provide thought leadership in selecting next-generation technologies and architecture components as per the latest trends and Scotiabank standards, frameworks, and best practices.
Promote a data-first mindset across the enterprise to enable Scotiabank to become a stronger data-driven organization.
Identify, monitor, and mitigate cross-project or cross-program dependencies while managing relationships, anticipating/mitigating risks, facilitating communications, and leading projects in an agile fashion.
Engage sponsoring executives and project team members, establishing trusted partnerships to ensure deliveries within scope, budget, and timelines while effectively communicating and discussing analytic insights with senior stakeholders.
Balance collaboration and consensus with the ability to assert project management discipline where required, while being a seasoned practitioner in leading project teams through fast and complex projects.
Work in an agile manner to onboard data, define ETL business processes, and create and manage a data dictionary and data lineage.
Lead a team of data engineers and full-stack developers.
Excel in relationship, stakeholder management, influencing, and negotiation skills, effective at all levels up to senior executives.
Efficiently perform management tasks including incident response and escalations, vendor and contract management, infrastructure management, service resiliency, and service ownership.
Enjoy the challenges of working on different types of projects (from large complex to simple).
Collaborate with various business functions to ensure Wealth Technology meets business needs.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

Minimum 10+ years in a data engineering-focused role.
Hands-on technical leadership with proven experience leading and mentoring engineering teams.
Expertise in implementing Google Cloud Platform (GCP) data services such as DataProc, Dataflow, CloudSQL, BigQuery, CloudSpanner in combination with third parties such as Spark, Apache Beam/Composer, DBT, Cloud PubSub, Confluent Kafka, Cloud Storage, Cloud Functions, and GitHub.
Experience with data streaming and technologies such as Kafka, Spark-streaming, etc.
Effective programming/query skills and in-depth knowledge of common data manipulation, visualization, and analytical tools (e.g., Python, Java, PowerBI, etc.).
Analytical, insights-driven with the ability to help the organization leverage data-driven decisions.
Strong architecture knowledge with experience in providing technical solutions for cloud infrastructure.
Active Google Cloud Data Engineer certification or Google Professional Cloud Architect certification.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.
Dynamic Ecosystem - Free tea & coffee, universal washrooms, and lots of space for team collaboration.
Community Engagement - We offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs such as hackathons.

Job Title: Director, Analytics and Business Services

Job Requisition ID: 89310

Ministry: Advanced Education

Location: Edmonton

Full or Part-Time: Full Time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Permanent

Scope: Open Competition

Closing Date: November 25, 2026

Classification: Management Senior Manager Zone 2

Salary: $5,139.3 to $6,526.16 bi-weekly ($134,135.73 - $170,332/year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

The Government of Alberta’s Ministry of Advanced Education
is responsible for Alberta’s adult learning and post-secondary education system, with a focus on making education accessible, affordable and high quality for Albertans.

To learn more about the Ministry of
Advanced Education
and what it has to offer, please follow the links: Advanced Education | Alberta.ca

Role Responsibilities

Are you a strategic leader who can turn complex data into insights that shape decisions? Join the Government of Alberta as Director, Analytics and Business Services, leading analytics, forecasting, research and corporate services that inform decisions across Alberta’s advanced education system.

Reporting to the Executive Director, DABS Branch, the Director provides strategic leadership for corporate services, advanced analytics, forecasting, labour market intelligence and research. The position oversees facilities, emergency management, business continuity and the deemed workers program while leading a multidisciplinary team responsible for data modernization, system forecasting, data analysis and evidence-based decision support.

The Director provides strategic advice to executive leadership, leads ministry-wide analytics initiatives, collaborates with government and external partners, and represents Alberta on national forums and committees.

Responsibilities Include
: -

Emergency & Business Continuity

Lead emergency management and business continuity programs.
Oversee emergency response and continuity plans.
Ensure regular training, exercises and readiness testing.
Coordinate with internal and post-secondary partners.
Represent the ministry on cross-government initiatives.
Ensure alignment with Government of Alberta requirements.

Facilities and Accommodation Strategy

Lead facilities and accommodation planning.
Oversee space planning, use, acquisition and disposal.
Provide strategic advice on efficient facility solutions.

Data Research

Set ministry-wide quantitative research priorities.
Lead cross-ministry data integration and collaboration.
Oversee federal and national data-sharing partnerships.
Advance automated analytics and reporting.
Ensure privacy, ethical data use and POPA compliance.

Forecasting & Strategic Intelligence

Develop models for enrolment, capacity and demographic trends.
Assess workforce demand, skills gaps and talent pipelines.
Model Student Aid, apprenticeship demand and financial risks.
Oversee performance indicators and accountability measures.
Translate analysis into actionable policy and investment advice.

Intergovernmental & Stakeholder Relation

Represent Alberta on national and FPT forums.
Lead negotiations on data sharing and apprenticeship mobility.
Provide strategic input on funding, education and labour market initiatives.
Build partnerships with post-secondary and research organizations.

Leadership & Operations

Lead multidisciplinary teams and strategic delivery.
Guide staff performance and development.
Oversee budgets, resources, procurement and contracts.
Approve key executive deliverables.
Act on behalf of the Executive Director when required.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Develop Networks

Build strong working relationships with Infrastructure and AEMA.

Creative Problem Solving

Deliver responsive solutions aligned with emergency management frameworks and department needs.

Systems Thinking

Lead the ministry’s research agenda across Alberta’s post-secondary and apprenticeship systems.

Agility

Provide guidance on facilities and accommodation processes and changes.

Qualifications

Veritree And Job Overview

veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.

veritree is seeking a Director, Operations to lead our Operations team: the glue that connects our teams and initiatives. Reporting to the COO, you will own veritree's Revenue Ops, Supply Ops, Business Ops, and Business Intelligence functions. These functions empower our Revenue, Forests, Product & Engineering, and Finance teams to operate as one business.

We sell verified trees sourced from planting partners worldwide, alongside new business lines in carbon, monitoring technology licensing, and nonprofit programs. That makes our business closer to a two-sided marketplace than pure SaaS: every customer commitment depends on supply, delivery, and data lining up behind it. As we move to a new AI-native platform, our Operations team is evolving into a team of operations engineers who build the tools, automations, and data flows the business runs on.

This is a hands-on role: you'll run operations first and then evolve the systems behind it. You inherit a capable team and working systems (several of which we've outgrown) and leave behind infrastructure the rest of the company can build upon. The role starts at Director-level, with room for advancement as determined by job performance and business needs.

12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)

Take the wheel: within your first 90 days, run the weekly operations cadence, own escalations across all four functions, and become the decision-maker on operational calls
Operating rhythm: set up how Operations runs for the next stage of the company: a clear meeting rhythm, defined team roles/decision rights, one agreed definition and owner for core metrics (pipeline, ACV, NRR, gross margin, tree inventory), and a 12-month operations roadmap signed off by executive leadership
Trusted data and reporting: keep commercial and delivery data clean across HubSpot, NetSuite, and the platform through go-live and beyond, and produce the monthly reporting pack and the operational metrics in board reporting from the BI stack
AI and automation: ship AI-powered tools and automations that measurably reduce manual work and save costs across the business

What You'll Do

Cross-Functional Operations

Run the operating cadence (meeting cadences, monthly business reviews, semi-annual planning) and the forums where Revenue, Forests, and Product & Engineering align on priorities
Own the deal desk with Sales, Customer Success, and Forests, so what we sell matches what we can deliver
Own the intake, prioritization, and SLA framework for operations requests from every team
Own operational readiness on the platform after go-live: close workflow gaps with Product & Engineering and lead change management
Make operational and commercial decisions within agreed guardrails (pricing, margin floors, custom deliverables), and escalate exceptions to executive leadership with a clear recommendation

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, coach, and develop the Operations team, including managers and individual contributors
Own hiring, onboarding, and ongoing performance management, in partnership with People Operations
Evolve the team into operations engineers by defining roles and scopes and building a culture that is both high-accountability and high-support

Revenue Operations

Own HubSpot as our commercial system of record, including deal stages, order and contract workflows, and clean handoffs between Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Finance
Own the customer revenue forecast and its methodology, in partnership with Finance and Revenue leadership
Own pricing discipline: the price sheet, margin floors, and a quarterly margin and pricing review
Own lead and sales funnel, retention, and unit-economics reporting

Supply Operations

Own demand and supply planning, translating the customer forecast into tree demand by ecosystem and region and partnering with Forests on sourcing and capacity
Own order management, inventory allocation, purchase orders, and fulfillment tracking, including future obligations to customers and planting partners, so every order is delivered on time against the right supply

Business Operations

Own the processes, policies, tooling, and Operations budget that keep the business running, and decide what gets automated and what stays manual
Run the OKR process and tracker, and support annual operating planning
Own the operating model for customer and partner site visits

Business Intelligence & Reporting

Own our data warehouse and BI layer, pulling from HubSpot, NetSuite, the platform, and planting data, as the single source of truth for operational metrics
Direct the team's AI agenda, shipping internal tools, agents, and workflow automations that measurably increase output across the business

Requirements

Qualifications

Professional Requirements Or Qualifications

8+ years in operations, including 3+ years leading a multi-function operations team (at least Revenue Operations and Business Operations) at a B2B company of roughly 75 to 250 people
Experience taking a company from founder-led, ad hoc operations to a repeatable operating system
Experience owning monthly and board-level operational reporting, including the data model and BI layer behind it
Strong HubSpot fluency (you know its strengths and its limits)
Fluency in commercial metrics: NRR, cohorts, funnel conversion, CAC and payback
Experience designing operating processes (intake, SLAs, deal desk) and leading change management for systems people use every day
You have an operating system (cadence, metric tree, single-owner accountability, an intake model) and can articulate it clearly
An AI-native way of working: you already use AI and automation to ship internal tools (e.g., n8n, AI agents)

Personal Strengths

An operator first: hands-on and low ego

Genuine passion for sustainability and nature-based solutions

new_jobs.description:
About Beacon:

Beacon is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies. They are niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently, accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.

The Role:

VieFund is a Beacon company with remote teams in Toronto, Ottawa and Vietnam. Its software is the system of record for mutual fund, segregated fund and GIC dealers in Canada: advisor tools, trades, settlements, account bookkeeping, and reporting, connected to the industry through FundServ, CANNEX and exempt-market dealer networks.

We are looking for the next technical leader of VieFund. You will own the platform end to end and work closely with the current technical team in Ottawa and Vietnam to build deep knowledge of the product, the dealers, and the operating rhythm. In the first year, you keep every dealer running through tax season, the FundServ standard change, and year-end, and you draw up the plan to move the platform off its on-prem footing, modernize it and add more value to customers with AI. You are the person who understands what is going on quickly and decides what to do about it.

You will be the technical owner of a profitable, long-held product with real customers and real seasonal deadlines, with Beacon's engineering leadership behind you and the mandate to make it better.

What You'll Do:

Own the VieFund platform end to end: architecture, codebase, database, releases, and production operations.
Build and maintain complete documentation of system behaviour, dealer configurations, and operational runbooks.
Maintain and evolve VieFund's FundServ integration, including annual standard upgrades, certification, and resolution of transaction and reconciliation issues with counterparties.
Design, build, and maintain the transaction processing, account bookkeeping, and reporting logic at the core of the product, ensuring accuracy and auditability.
Act as the final escalation point for client-facing technical issues; diagnose root causes and implement durable fixes.
Plan and deliver around the industry calendar, including tax season, RRSP and RRIF deadlines, and regulatory and standards changes.
Define and execute the technical roadmap, including the migration from on-prem infrastructure to the cloud and the adoption of modern engineering and AI-assisted development practices.
Manage production environments across hosted and client-managed Windows Server deployments, including backups, patching, security, and uptime.
Partner with hosting providers, dealers, and internal stakeholders to deliver reliable service and clear communication.
Hire, mentor, and lead engineers and contractors as the team grows.

What we are looking for:

Must have:

Deep, hands-on FundServ experience. Not just sending and receiving files: you have lived through the yearly standard change, you have debugged failures that originated at other vendors or at the fund, and you know how to work the problem when the documentation does not help.
Mutual fund transaction accounting and reporting. You understand the bookkeeping behind trades, settlements, distributions, and corrections, and you have fixed it when it was wrong.
Expert in .NET, MSSQL, and T-SQL. Much of the dealer-specific logic lives in stored procedures and scripts. You are at home there.
Windows Server management. You can stand up, patch, back up, and troubleshoot production servers, including ones you do not control.
Able to be in Ottawa at least bi-weekly for the first six months as part of onboarding. Knowledge transfer happens in person.
Judgment that does not need a committee. You will often be the only engineer in the room.
Easy to work with. Dealers call when something is wrong. The team has to trust you with the product.
Daily use of AI coding tools, and the drive to bring them into a codebase that has none.

Nice to have:

Experience migrating an on-prem system to the cloud, and the judgement to sequence it without breaking customers.
FIX protocol, for the ETF side of the business. Small part of the work, easy to pick up, but a head start helps.
Experience at a Canadian wealth or dealer platform (back office, transfer agency, or dealer software).
Experience replacing a long-tenured sole owner of a system.

Location and Working Arrangement:

Remote with ability to meet with with the teams in Ottawa and/or Toronto, Ontario. During onboarding must be able to be in Ottawa bi-weekly for the first 6 months.
Some work happens outside dealer business hours so it does not disrupt their day. Expect occasional evenings and weekends, heaviest around the seasonal peaks. Reducing this is part of the modernization mandate, but it is the reality today.

Our Values at Beacon Software

Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.
Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.
Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process:
To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions:
Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

Reporting to the Executive Director, DABS Branch, the Director provides strategic leadership for corporate services, advanced analytics, forecasting, labour market intelligence and research. The position oversees facilities, emergency management, business continuity and the deemed workers program while leading a multidisciplinary team responsible for data modernization, system forecasting, data analysis and evidence-based decision support.

The Director provides strategic advice to executive leadership, leads ministry-wide analytics initiatives, collaborates with government and external partners, and represents Alberta on national forums and committees.

: -

Oversee emergency response and continuity plans.
Ensure regular training, exercises and readiness testing.

Represent the ministry on cross-government initiatives.
Ensure alignment with Government of Alberta requirements.

Oversee space planning, use, acquisition and disposal.
Provide strategic advice on efficient facility solutions.

Data Research

Set ministry-wide quantitative research priorities.
Lead cross-ministry data integration and collaboration.
Oversee federal and national data-sharing partnerships.
Advance automated analytics and reporting.
Ensure privacy, ethical data use and POPA compliance.

Model Student Aid, apprenticeship demand and financial risks.
Oversee performance indicators and accountability measures.
Translate analysis into actionable policy and investment advice.

Lead negotiations on data sharing and apprenticeship mobility.
Provide strategic input on funding, education and labour market initiatives.
Build partnerships with post-secondary and research organizations.

Lead multidisciplinary teams and strategic delivery.
Guide staff performance and development.
Oversee budgets, resources, procurement and contracts.
Approve key executive deliverables.
Act on behalf of the Executive Director when required.

Build strong working relationships with Infrastructure and AEMA.

Deliver responsive solutions aligned with emergency management frameworks and department needs.

Systems Thinking

Lead the ministry’s research agenda across Alberta’s post-secondary and apprenticeship systems.

Agility

University Graduation in a field related to the position assignment, supplemented by six years progressively responsible experience.

Several years of progressive leadership and management experience.
Strong knowledge of Government of Alberta legislation, policies and priorities, including emergency management and ATIA/POPA requirements.
Experience leading complex projects and multidisciplinary teams.
Strong data analysis, research and interpretation skills.

Experience managing budgets, contracts, grants and RFP processes.
Strong strategic planning, project management and coordination skills.
Demonstrated ability to lead innovation, transformation and organizational change.
Excellent communication, presentation, facilitation and stakeholder relationship skills.

Strong political acumen, critical thinking and problem-solving skills.

Company Description
Mallette is a leading professional services firm with over 40 offices across multiple regions of Québec and more than 1,600 team members working in diverse sectors. The firm is recognized for its strong training culture, deep expertise, and commitment to client service, positioning its professionals as trusted advisors of choice. Mallette continually strengthens its leadership position by being part of TIAG (The International Accounting Group), an international alliance that enables clients to receive high-quality support for their business activities outside Canada from local experts at reasonable costs. Through this alliance, Mallette maintains its unique identity and independence while expanding its reach. Role Description
The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) at Mallette provides strategic leadership and oversight of the firm’s overall direction, performance, and growth. In this part-time, remote role, the CEO will define and implement long-term business and financial strategies, align operations with organizational goals, and ensure consistent delivery of high-quality services to clients. The CEO will collaborate with senior leaders and partners to manage budgets, monitor key performance indicators, and drive operational efficiency across offices and service lines. Daily responsibilities include guiding business planning initiatives, supporting expansion within Québec and internationally through the TIAG alliance, and fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, and client-centricity. The CEO will also represent the firm with key stakeholders, including clients, partners, and external organizations, while upholding Mallette’s values and independence.

Ability to lead remotely, build strong teams, and promote a collaborative, inclusive, and ethical work environment.
